With \(q=n-r\), the source identifies \(A:=\Lambda/I_{r,q}\) as a quotient whose surviving Schur classes are those indexed by \(\lambda\subseteq q^r\), and states that \[ J_v\subseteq A \quad\text{is generated as an ideal by}\quad \{s_\mu:i^j\subseteq\mu\subseteq q^r\}. \] [source-2@L1310-L1324|claim=formal-document] [source-2@L1365-L1375|claim=formal-document]

claims.text: Assume \(1\le i\le q\), \(1\le j\le r\), set \(d_0=ij\), \(D=rq\), and define, for each integer \(d\), \[ B_d:=\{\lambda:\ i^j\subseteq\lambda\subseteq q^r,\ |\lambda|=d\}, \qquad m_d:=|B_d|. \] The degree-\(d\) part of \(J_v\) is \[ (J_v)_d=\bigoplus_{\lambda\in B_d}\mathbb Zs_\lambda. \] Explicitly, the displayed generators give the inclusion from right to left. Conversely, the Littlewood--Richardson expansion \[ s_\alpha s_\mu=\sum_{\lambda}c_{\alpha\mu}^{\lambda}s_\lambda \] has \(c_{\alpha\mu}^{\lambda}=0\) unless \(\mu\subseteq\lambda\); thus multiplication of a class containing \(i^j\) produces only classes containing \(i^j\), with classes outside \(q^r\) zero in \(A\). The Schur classes in \(q^r\) are linearly independent, so the sum is direct. Let \[ T_d:=\{(k,\alpha,\mu):1\le k\le d-d_0,\ \alpha\subseteq q^r,\ |\alpha|=k,\ \mu\in B_{d-k}\}, \qquad s_d:=|T_d|. \] Define the integer matrix \[ R_d:\mathbb Z^{s_d}\longrightarrow\mathbb Z^{m_d} \] using the bases \(T_d\) and \(B_d\), respectively, by \[ (R_d)_{\lambda,(k,\alpha,\mu)}=c_{\alpha\mu}^{\lambda} \qquad(\lambda\in B_d). \] Thus its column indexed by \((k,\alpha,\mu)\) is the Schur-coordinate vector of \(s_\alpha s_\mu\). Since the image of \(\Lambda_+\) in \(A\) is \(A_+\), \[ (\Lambda_+J_v)_d=(A_+J_v)_d=\operatorname{im}R_d, \qquad (J_v/\Lambda_+J_v)_d\cong\operatorname{coker}R_d. \] Consequently, for prescribed \(N_d\ge0\), \[ (J_v/\Lambda_+J_v)_d\cong\mathbb Z^{N_d} \iff \operatorname{rank}R_d=m_d-N_d \ \text{and every nonzero Smith factor of }R_d\text{ is }1. \] For \(d<d_0\) or \(d>D\), \(B_d=T_d=\varnothing\), so \(m_d=s_d=0\), \(R_d:0\to0\), and the quotient degree is \(0\). At \(d=d_0\), \(B_{d_0}=\{i^j\}\), \(T_{d_0}=\varnothing\), and \(R_{d_0}:0\to\mathbb Z\), so the quotient degree is canonically \(\mathbb Z[s_{i^j}]\). Globally, with \[ R:=\bigoplus_{d=d_0}^{D}R_d,\qquad m:=\sum_{d=d_0}^{D}m_d,\qquad N:=\sum_{d=d_0}^{D}N_d, \] one has \[ J_v/\Lambda_+J_v\cong\operatorname{coker}R. \] Thus the preceding rank-plus-Smith criterion applies to this finite block-diagonal presentation. No ranks or Smith factors for general parameters are asserted here.
